Resolves #19076

A Workstation pop-out transfers its item out of the source document's catalog. Header publication previously omitted that item, leaving the old source edge in the provider's merged data. The publisher now sets departed local items' `edge` to `null` in its existing batch, preserving their other fields and the popup provider's own header state.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). Prescription checked: `HeaderActionPolicy.publishDocument` owns this derived workspace-local edge; the Provider merge and transfer executor contracts are unchanged. `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; local pre-commit checks passed.

Evidence: L3 (unchanged real Workstation popup witness on the committed source; unit proof uses the real transfer operation) → L3 required. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — retire source edge, preserve other fields/target state | CI-covered: new `DockHeaderState.spec.mjs` arm uses `Operations.transferItem`, checks source catalog removal, preserved source flags, independent target edge and no tombstone for an inherited parent item. |
| AC-2 — red/green regression and unchanged no-op behavior | Outside-CI red control: added transfer arm failed before the fix (`right` vs `null`). CI-covered: the owning header-state suite retains its formatter-count/no-op controls. |
| AC-3 — unchanged full popup witness | Outside-CI: `WorkstationHeaderStatePopOutNL.spec.mjs` **1 passed**, including retained provider/flags, edge `right → null`, popup adoption and native close. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. Prior item keys are read from the LOCAL `dock.items` config, so publishing a popup's document cannot retire keys merely inherited from its parent. No pane-provider rebinding, flag synchronization or general data deletion is introduced.

## Test Evidence

- Base `633585423d`: whole header-state popup witness failed at its original `after.truth` assertion, `edge: right` instead of `null`.
- Repaired source: `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<Brain checkout> npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationHeaderStatePopOutNL.spec.mjs --workers=1` → **1 passed**, 1.7s test / 3.6s run. Receipt shows the same provider and all other fields unchanged; no error-guard waiver.
- The transfer unit arm was run before the production edit and failed on that same stale edge; normal publication and provider isolation controls remain in the owning CI suite.

## Post-Merge Validation

None required for this bounded repair. Broader popup identity/row-pool and film work remain outside this leaf under #17844.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19076 (body, Contract Ledger, ACs); dev `HeaderActionPolicy#publishDocument` (`:296-340`); `state.Provider` `getDataConfig` (`:595`), `internalSetData` (`:765-822`, the parent-object bubbling) and `processDataObject` (`:862`); `core.Config#set` (`:154-169`); your subtask trace in Memory Core.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The next publication must write `edge: null` into this provider for every item it previously published that is absent from the new document, in the same batched write. Other leaves stay, and nothing inherited from a parent provider may be retired into a child. It must not hardcode a merge-semantics change in Provider. The isolation should use a real `Operations.transferItem` across a parent and a child provider.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `getDataConfig('dock.items')?.get()` reads `#dataConfigs` directly (`Provider.mjs:596`), with no parent walk, and intermediate paths hold their merged object. So the prior set is exactly this provider's own items. The retirement rides the existing `setDataAtSameLevel` call.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The fix follows a traced mechanism (merge-without-delete, `Operations.transferItem` removing the source record), not the symptom.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge** (non-blocking, *hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation*): your trace says the retained pane's `closestProvider` stays cached on the source workspace's provider after the hop. After this PR its `edge` is correct, but the other leaves it reads (`locked`, `pinnable`, `closable`) are still the source's copies. If the target workspace later changes one, say a lock in the popup, the pane would read the stale source value. #19076 scopes pane provider rebinding and flag sync out, and no open ticket owns either (searched). If you can observe it, a `defect-note` is enough to keep it from being lost.
- **Documented search:** I looked for three regressions and found none:
  - the unchanged republish now re-sets each retired item's `edge: null`, but `Config#set` returns before `notify` when `isEqual(null, null)` (`Config.mjs:162`), so the leaf stays a no-op and AC-2 holds by construction;
  - a pane-contract-only item (`publishPaneContract` writes `reloadable` before any document) gains an `edge: null` leaf on the next publication, which reads the same as `undefined` to the pin binding (`!field(...)`);
  - retired entries are never pruned, so the provider keeps one per item that ever left, which is bounded by the items that passed through.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: `Provider#setDataAtSameLevel` merges leaves recursively, so omitting a key never deletes it. Any publisher that projects a shrinking set onto a provider has to retire what left, as this one now does.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: N/A
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Retire the leaf the workspace owned, not the item record the pane still reads. That kept the fix at six lines without touching Provider semantics.
